name: AI Layoff Trap
blurb: Falk & Tsoukalas closed-form Nash vs. cooperative automation rates per sector.
mechanism:
Each sector is modelled as N symmetric firms each choosing an automation rate α_i ∈ [0,1]. Sector demand D falls in the average automation rate, generating a negative externality between firms — automating cuts your costs but shrinks everyone's revenue.

Closing the first-order conditions in α yields a single algebraic system: `n_star` solves for the symmetric Nash α, `coop_alpha` solves for the cooperative (joint-profit-maximising) α, and `wedge = nash_alpha − coop_alpha` measures how much firms over-automate at equilibrium. The model is purely analytical — no simulation, no Monte Carlo — so each forecast checkpoint is effectively a parameter refit and a closed-form re-solve.

Per-sector inputs (N, marginal cost saving from automation, demand elasticity, outside-option wage) come from the cosmos seed via `extract_firm_params`, which projects company filings into the `FirmParams` shape the solver expects.
